declared: Thresholds and definitions below are declared BEFORE the tool is run on the study checkpoints and are fixed; the tool reports against them and never adjusts them. The diagnostics describe the saved bootstrap estimates; they do not change, replace or filter any original result, flag, interval or criterion. Existing Batch C flag definitions (config/bootstrap_protocol.json, scientific_validity) are preserved and reported unchanged.

inputs.read: the saved target checkpoints of a Batch C run (checkpoints/CKPT__<target_id>.rds: replicate estimates, per-replicate failure reasons, three logical diagnostic vectors, complete-case counts, seconds, and the one-row original summary) and the run's aggregate tables bootstrap_summary.csv, bootstrap_validity.csv, bootstrap_point_estimates.csv, batch_c_metadata.json, RUN_MANIFEST.csv
inputs.not_read: participant data, the canonical CSV, resample indices (not stored), anything that would allow a sample to be reconstructed or a model to be refitted; the tool contains no fitting code and no data-import code (checked by a test)
inputs.outputs: aggregate tables only: no replicate-level estimate is exported

scope.expected_note: expectations come from the Phase 3C.1 review; a mismatch is reported as a NOTE, not changed

estimate_handling.classes: each saved estimate is exactly one of: finite; NA (a failed refit: missing); NaN; +Inf or -Inf. Counts of every class are reported separately and must add up to the number of attempted replicates.
estimate_handling.finite_set: the finite estimates are the 'successful refits' of the original rule (is.finite); every diagnostic below uses this set unless stated otherwise

extremeness_diagnostics.label: COEFFICIENT-BASED EXTREMENESS DIAGNOSTICS. A flag means that a saved estimate is large by the stated definition. It is NOT confirmed separation: fitted probabilities and fits are not available.
extremeness_diagnostics.notation: e = a finite replicate estimate; p = the primary M2-L coefficient of the target; s = the reference SE of the target (HC3 SE for continuous outcomes, model-based Wald SE for the binary outcome; both as recorded in the run's bootstrap_validity.csv); m = median of the finite estimates; MAD = 1.4826 x median(|e - m|) (scaled MAD)

definitions.note: magnitude no plausible log-odds per exposure unit; typical of divergent fits
PRIMARY DIAGNOSTIC DEFINITION used for tail ranks and omission summaries unless stated otherwise
robust outlier; not evaluated (reported as not evaluable) when MAD = 0

extremeness_diagnostics.overlap: overlap of each definition with the saved glm_not_converged, level_absent and other_aliased vectors is reported (counts only)

distribution_summaries.quantile_type_note: descriptive quantiles use R's default type 7; the ORIGINAL percentile limits are always type 8 and are reconstructed separately
distribution_summaries.statistics: n by class, median, IQR (type 7), MAD (raw and scaled), SD of the finite estimates, SD after omitting the X2 estimates, minimum, maximum, the selected quantiles, tail ranges: q0.975 - q0.5, q0.5 - q0.025, max - q0.975, q0.025 - min, and the ratios SD/s, (IQR/1.349)/s, scaled MAD/s and (q0.975 - q0.025)/(2 * 1.96 * s); the original Batch C SD-ratio flag value is recomputed from the checkpoints and compared with the run's recorded value

percentile_reconstruction.rule: the original 95% percentile limits: stats::quantile(finite estimates, c(0.025, 0.975), type = 8) when at least 20 estimates are finite, otherwise missing; also computed with an independent type-8 implementation
percentile_reconstruction.compared_with: the one-row summary stored in the checkpoint and the run's bootstrap_summary.csv; exact (bitwise) agreement is reported separately
percentile_reconstruction.ranks: for the lower and upper limit, the type-8 order-statistic positions j and j + 1 (j = floor(n p + (p + 1)/3 + 4 eps)); the number and share of flagged estimates among the order statistics at or beyond each limit (lowest j + 1 and highest n - j), and whether either order statistic that defines a limit is itself flagged

omission_sensitivity.label: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY. Limits recomputed after omitting the flagged estimates (type 8, at least 20 remaining) never replace the original intervals.
omission_sensitivity.reported: per target and definition: number omitted, filtered limits, change in each limit (absolute, relative to the original interval width, and in units of s), and whether the interval's inclusion of zero changes

provenance.checkpoint_hashes: SHA-256 of every checkpoint file, recorded before and after the audit (read-only check: the audit must leave every checkpoint unchanged)
provenance.signature_check: each checkpoint carries a signature = string hash of (input hash | configuration hash | protocol hash | package-source fingerprint of the ORIGINAL run | target id | seed | replicates); the tool recomputes it from the run's recorded metadata
provenance.original_run: batch_c_metadata.json hashes, RUN_MANIFEST verification, the original run's source fingerprint compared with the audit tool's own source manifest (differences are expected and listed)
provenance.tool_source: SHA-256 source manifest and fingerprint of the diagnostic tool's package source, computed at start and end of the audit; changes during the run are reported
known_unavailable_evidence: checkpoint creation time inside the file (only the file-system modification time exists)
the original run manifest does not list the checkpoint files, so the checkpoint hashes cannot be verified against an original hash list; the recorded hashes document the state at audit time
per-replicate fitted probabilities or model fits (separation cannot be confirmed)
the end-of-run source manifest of the original run
the signature is a non-cryptographic string hash: it binds a checkpoint to the recorded run parameters but is not tamper-proof

statuses.CHECKPOINT_INTEGRITY: all 180 checkpoints present, readable, schema-valid (only the declared fields, no data frame other than the one-row summary), unique, consistent lengths, estimate classes consistent with the failure reasons, signature recomputed and matching; no unexpected checkpoint files
statuses.CHECKPOINTS_UNCHANGED: SHA-256 of every checkpoint identical before and after
statuses.ACCOUNTING: for every target n_finite + n_NA + n_NaN + n_Inf = attempted, and the counts equal the run's summary (successful, failed)
statuses.QUANTILE_RECONSTRUCTION: the reconstructed type-8 limits and median equal the stored summary and the run's summary within the declared tolerance for all 180 targets
statuses.ORIGINAL_RUN_PROVENANCE: the original run's manifest verifies and its metadata hashes are present
statuses.SOURCE_INTEGRITY: the audit tool's package source did not change during the audit
statuses.EXTREMENESS_DIAGNOSTICS: descriptive only (counts of targets with extreme estimates by definition); not a pass/fail status
